\subsection{Models undercount repetitions, proportionally}

Figure~\ref{fig:main}(a) shows the relative count error against $k$. Below
$k\!=\!6$ every model is essentially exact; from $k\!=\!6$ the panel splits.
Pooled at $k\ge6$, repeated items are rendered with a median error of
\ErrRep{}\% $[\ErrRepLo{}, \ErrRepHi{}]$ ($n=\ErrRepN{}$), one-directional:
models produce \emph{fewer} repetitions than requested, never systematically
more.

Its \emph{shape}, however, is not the one Theorem~\ref{thm:collapse}(iv)
predicts, and that is this paper's main negative result. A finite $N^\ast$ implies
saturation: past it no Lipschitz readout separates counts, so a decoder asked for
ever more should keep emitting about $N^\ast$. Fitting the panel's median count
above $k\!=\!6$ against a constant gives residual sum of squares \ShapeSatSSE{},
against $\hat c=bk$ only \ShapePropSSE{} with $b=\ShapePropSlope{}$ --- the count
tracks the request at \ShapePropPct{}\% of it, in \ShapePropModels{} of
\ErrNModels{} checkpoints individually. The interpolating form $\hat
c(k)=N^\ast(1-e^{-k/N^\ast})$, free to find a horizon if one is there, puts
$N^\ast$ at \ShapeNStarMin{}--\ShapeNStarMax{}, at or beyond our ladder's top.
Within $k\le32$ there is no counting horizon, and we report the theorem's
consequence as \emph{not observed} rather than confirmed.

What degrades with $k$ is reliability, not proportion: the share rendered
\emph{exactly} right falls from \ExactRepKLo{}\% at $k\!=\!\ExactRepKLoVal{}$ to
\ExactRepKHi{}\% at $k\!=\!\ExactRepKHiVal{}$ while the median error holds near a
tenth. \ErrBestModel{} shows no deficit at all; the theorem is silent about such
a model, since without contraction no horizon follows. The effect separates from
its own control in \ErrNSep{} of \ErrNModels{} checkpoints, and holds whether the
repeated unit is a word, a sentence or a place-value pattern.

\subsection{The limit is periodicity, not length}

Figure~\ref{fig:main}(b) is the paper's sharpest test. Each control has its
twin's carrier and word count, differing only in that the $k$ copies of one word
become $k$ distinct words. Were the failure about sequence length, attention span
or exposure bias, the curves would coincide. They do not: at $k\ge6$ the median
control error is \ErrCtl{}\% $[\ErrCtlLo{}, \ErrCtlHi{}]$ over $n=\ErrCtlN{}$
generations, at every $k$ up to $32$, for every model. The contrast is sharpest
in exactly-correct renderings --- \ExactCtl{}\% for controls against
\ExactRep{}\% for their twins: the same decoders that miscount a repeated
sequence five times in six get thirty-two \emph{different} words right nineteen
times in twenty. Controls are not perfect --- the residual \CtlMissPct{}\% carry
genuine truncations --- but they are exact where the repeated items are not.

Two rival explanations --- that repeated text is simply improbable, and that the
attractor is acoustic rather than text-side --- are ruled out by their own
predictions (S8).

\subsection{The decoder buys states more slowly under repetition}

Theorem~\ref{thm:collapse}(ii) says states visited under periodic conditioning
stop being mutually distinguishable, so more repetitions should buy distinct
internal states more slowly than the same amount of non-repetitive text does. We
count states by the effective rank $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{eff}} = \exp(-\sum_i p_i
\log p_i)$ of the trajectory over normalised singular values; the statistic is
the \emph{capacity gain}
$\mathrm{d}\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{eff}}/\mathrm{d}\log k$, bootstrapped over
templates.

Figure~\ref{fig:main}(c,d) shows the result. On repeated text the capacity gain
is a factor \CapRatio{} of the control gain, with disjoint 95\% intervals for
\CapSepPhrase{} panel checkpoints; the matched-pair form of
the comparison gives a positive gap in \CapFracPos{}\% of pairs.

An obvious objection is circularity: correctly rendering \emph{very} sixteen
times really does produce monotonous audio, so a low-rank trajectory might follow
from the stimulus rather than from lost capacity. It does not. Adding realised
output diversity (type/token ratio over emitted tokens, adjacent-repeat rate,
length) as covariates leaves the ratio at \CapAdjRatio{}; restricting to items
rendered \emph{correctly} leaves it at \CapCorrRatio{}. The gain stays
\emph{positive} in \CapPosModels{} of \ErrNModels{} checkpoints: repetition
slows state acquisition rather than halting it, where a decoder at the fixed
point would gain none --- the count curve's message again, approach rather than
arrival. A probe accordingly finds the count degraded, not erased (Section~5).

Lemma~\ref{lem:dilution} concerns the softmax \emph{restricted to the $k$
repeated keys}. Renormalised over those columns, profile entropy grows with
$\log k$ at slope \BlockEntropySlope{} and the most-attended occurrence holds
$\ShareMedK{}/k$ of the block's mass typically, $\ShareMaxK{}/k$ at worst: the
extreme spread Assumption~\ref{ass:periodic} needs is $\delta\le\DeltaMax{}$
nats, so attention is near-uniform typically but not uniformly so (S6).
Qwen3-TTS sums text and acoustic embeddings per position, so the lemma cannot be
checked there.
